//: Defaults for the 'Publish to Remote Server' task (.vscode/deploy-remote.ps1). Don't put your values here: the first run copies this file to deploy-remote.local.json (git-ignored), and that copy is the one to edit. A key missing from the local copy falls back to the value here. {Server} and {SiteName} are replaced in the URL and path values.
//Method: Share = mirror the build into a network share of the server's IIS site folder (no remote services needed). WebDeploy = msdeploy to the server's Web Deploy endpoint.
//SharePath: Share: UNC path of the share that points at the IIS site's physical folder (the folder holding web.config).
//WebDeployUrl: WebDeploy: the Web Management Service handler on port 8172 (needs the IIS Management Service feature + remote connections enabled + Web Deploy's IIS Deployment Handler on the server). Alternative: the Remote Agent Service, http://{Server}/MSDEPLOYAGENTSERVICE with AuthType NTLM (UserName must be an admin on the server).
//UserName: Account on the server, e.g. SERVER\you or you@outlook.com. Leave blank to use your current Windows login. The password is prompted for, never stored here; RememberPassword saves it encrypted for your Windows account only in deploy-remote.local.secret.
//ServiceAdminUserName: 'Publish to Remote Server (service)' only: an ADMINISTRATOR account on the server for PowerShell remoting, which runs install-service.ps1 there. Blank = UserName. Its password is kept apart from UserName's (deploy-remote.local.admin.secret) when the names differ.
//ServerAppPath: The app folder as the server sees it (e.g. C:\inetpub\OmniCard). Blank = the folder behind SharePath's share.
//PreserveSettings: Top-level appsettings.json sections the server keeps between deploys. New keys from the repo's appsettings.json still flow through.
